日.meaning: A tall window with one bar across the middle, and the <part>sun</part> blazing in it. It glows at dawn, goes dark at dusk, and glows again the next morning. One trip of the sun past that window is one <kanji>day</kanji>.
日.on: The sun warms your k<sound>nee</sound> all afternoon while a <sound>chee</sound>tah naps across your lap.
日.kun: The sun peeks in through the window bars and giggles: '<sound>Hee</sound>!'

一.meaning: A single flat plank lies on the ground: no second plank, no post, nothing on top. Hold up a finger to count it. It's the <part>one</part> plank, and you'll find it inside lots of other kanji, always meaning <kanji>one</kanji>.
一.on: A plank bridge just wide enough for one. An <sound>ea</sound>gle lands on it, then a <sound>chee</sound>tah steps on, and crack! Room for one only.
一.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>!' giggles the chef, setting down one lonely cube of <sound>to</sound>fu on a huge plate.

人.meaning: Two sticks lean on each other so they won't fall over. Kick one and both topple; together they stand, and even start to stroll away on their own two legs. That walking pair of sticks is the <part>person</part> shape: a <kanji>person</kanji>.
人.on: The stick person chews on a knobbly <sound>gin</sound>ger root and sneezes so hard it nearly falls apart.
人.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>!' giggles the stick person, peeking out from behind a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

大.meaning: A man spreads his arms as wide as they'll go and plants his legs apart: 'The fish I caught was THIS big!' He fills the whole doorway. With every retelling the fish grows, and so do his arms. Everything about it is <kanji>large</kanji>.
大.on: To prove it, he rolls a pair of <sound>di</sound>ce, each one as big as a fridge.
大.kun: '<sound>Ohh</sound>!' gasps the crowd, long and slow, as the fish in the story gets bigger and bigger.

手.meaning: A hooked post with three bars across it and a little curl on top stands up and waves at you. The bars wiggle like fingers, the curl flicks like a thumb. It wants a high five: it's a <kanji>hand</kanji>.
手.on: The hand grabs a fistful of <sound>su</sound>gar cubes and won't let go.
手.kun: The hand pats a <sound>te</sound>ddy bear gently on the head.

下.meaning: A <part>faucet</part> hangs upside down under a <part>one</part>-plank shelf, dripping on everything beneath it. Whatever is down there gets wet. That's what you get for standing <kanji>below</kanji>.
下.on: A <sound>ca</sound>rp swims in a bucket below the dripping faucet, mouth open, catching every drop.
下.kun: <sound>She</sound> drops her <sound>ta</sound>co, and it lands on the floor far below, right under the drip.

車.meaning: From a bridge you look straight down on it: a box seat, one long axle stabbing through the middle, a bar of wheels at the front and another at the back. It honks at you. It's a <kanji>car</kanji>.
車.on: A <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock lands on the car's roof and rides along all the way to town.
車.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo drives the car, a kanga<sound>roo</sound> sits in the back, and both wave to <sound>Ma</sound> as they speed past.

行.meaning: On the left a <part>chairlift</part> rattles past; on the right stands a signpost with two arms and a hooked foot. Together they make a busy <part>crossroads</part> where nobody stops: skiers jump off the chairlift and keep <kanji>going</kanji>, left, right or straight on.
行.on: Every skier grabs an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne at the crossroads and eats it on the move.
行.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals a skier as the chairlift tips her off, and away she goes down the slope.

子.meaning: A round little head, arms flung out wide, one hooked leg kicking at the floor: someone tiny is in the middle of a tantrum. They will not eat their peas. It's a <kanji>child</kanji>.
子.on: The child hides behind a toy <sound>shi</sound>eld and throws the peas over the top.
子.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala climbs onto the child's back and won't let go.

女.meaning: A figure flings her arms out and bends her knees low, legs crossed, balancing on one foot. She holds the pose for a whole minute while the crowd claps and the judges gasp. She's a <kanji>woman</kanji> with very strong legs.
女.on: A <sound>jo</sound>gger runs laps around her the whole time, trying to make her wobble.
女.kun: <sound>On</sound>ly she can balance a stack of <sound>na</sound>an on her head while standing on one foot.

今.meaning: An <part>umbrella</part> pops open over a <part>one</part>-plank bench, and a little zigzag of lightning strikes the ground right under it. The storm starts this very second. Don't wait: get under it <kanji>now</kanji>!
今.on: A giant <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down and squeezes under the umbrella with you.
今.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k! <sound>Ma</sound>, now!' yells the kid, diving under the umbrella as the lightning strikes.

食.meaning: Under an <part>umbrella</part> roof sits a bowl of steaming white rice with a spoon stuck in it. Rain pours down all around, but nobody cares: you sit under the umbrella and <kanji>eat</kanji> every grain.
食.on: Every time the chef tastes the stew, his hair springs straight up in a wild <sound>shock</sound>.
食.kun: Rice finished, you start on a crunchy <sound>ta</sound>co, still under the umbrella.

口.meaning: A tiny square <part>cage</part> with nothing inside sits on the table. Then it opens and closes, opens and closes, and starts asking for snacks. It was never a cage at all: it's a <kanji>mouth</kanji>.
口.on: The mouth gulps down a whole ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in one bite.
口.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the mouth, holding a lump of <sound>chee</sound>se.

何.meaning: Next to a <part>coat hook</part> hangs an <part>approval</part> sign: a mouth under a little shelf that says yes to everything. Hang a hat on the hook, and the mouth nods. Hang a dripping fish on it, and the mouth finally frowns: '<kanji>What</kanji>? What is that thing?'
何.on: A <sound>ca</sound>rp flops out from behind the shelf. 'What? What is a fish doing here?'
何.kun: 'What's for dinner?' asks the mouth. Just <sound>naan</sound>, a flat bread as wide as the shelf.

上.meaning: A <part>faucet</part> stands on a <part>one</part>-plank floor and sprays straight up like a fountain. The water shoots higher than the roof and rains down on the birds flying <kanji>above</kanji>.
上.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey jumps out of its mother's pouch and rides the fountain high into the air.
上.kun: '<sound>Ooh</sound>! <sound>Eh</sound>?' says a bird up above, as the spray hits its tail feathers.

牛.meaning: Two bars on a tall post, and a little slash poking up on top like one bent horn. Stare at it across the field and it stares right back, chewing slowly, then lets out a long moo. It's a <kanji>cow</kanji>.
牛.on: Two farmers ar<sound>gue</sound> about whose cow is louder, and the cow moos over both of them.
牛.kun: '<sound>Ooh</sound>, <sound>shee</sound>p!' says the cow, and trots off to join the flock.

物.meaning: A <part>cow</part> grabs a <part>broom</part> and sweeps out the barn. Out of the straw come all sorts of things: a boot, a spoon, a lost key, a clock. The cow piles them up and calls each one a <kanji>thing</kanji>.
物.on: The first thing it sweeps up is a toy <sound>bu</sound>ll, and the dust makes the cow sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
物.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le pops out of the pile of things and squeaks: '<sound>No</sound>, those are mine!'

気.meaning: <part>Steam</part> curls up from a hot bath, and a pair of <part>scissors</part> hides inside it, blades open in a tiny X. Snip, snip: they cut the steam into the shape of a ghost, which sighs happily and drifts about. You can't see it, but you can feel its <kanji>spirit</kanji>.
気.on: The ghost unlocks the bathroom door with a brass <sound>key</sound> and drifts out in the steam.
気.kun: The spirit hums one high note, '<sound>Kee</sound>!', and the steam swirls around it.

入.meaning: Two strokes lean in and touch at the top: a narrow <part>entrance</part>, just big enough to squeeze through. Duck your head, turn sideways and slide in. You have found the way to <kanji>enter</kanji>.
入.on: Inside the narrow door, a waiter hands you a me<sound>nu</sound> as long as your arm.
入.kun: '<sound>Hi</sound>!' says someone already inside, as you squeeze in through the door.

乗.meaning: A tall stalk of <part>grain</part> has a <part>one</part>-plank seat nailed across its stem, with little footrests sticking out each side. A mouse climbs on, grabs the drooping top like reins, and off the stalk sways across the field. Hop on and <kanji>ride</kanji>!
乗.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops on behind the mouse, and the grain stalk bends almost to the ground.
乗.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' squeaks the mouse, as the joey's mother tries to climb on too.

用.meaning: Nobody throws out this old <part>fence</part> panel. Hang coats on its bars, prop it up as a shelf, lay it flat as a bridge over a puddle. Whatever the job, you find a way to <kanji>utilize</kanji> it.
用.on: Hang a <sound>yo</sound>-yo from one of its bars, and the fence is a toy too.
用.kun: The fence panel even works as a tray for a row of sticky <sound>mochi</sound> cakes.

通.meaning: Someone drops a giant <part>padlock</part> at the top of the <part>ramp</part>, and every driver slows down to stare. Horns honk, cars inch round it one by one, and soon they're stuck nose to tail all the way down. It's rush-hour <kanji>traffic</kanji>.
通.on: Exhaust fumes everywhere: one driver lets out a long, slow sneeze, '<sound>Tsooo</sound>!', that rattles every window in the jam.
通.kun: A car rolls over your <sound>toe</sound> as it finally squeezes through.

木.meaning: A straight trunk, one crossbar of branches, and two roots digging into the dirt below. Birds perch on the crossbar, a squirrel runs up the trunk, and a dog sniffs every root. It's a <kanji>tree</kanji>.
木.on: The squirrel wears a tiny <sound>moc</sound>casin on each paw to climb the tree quietly.
木.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird pecks at the roots, looking for worms.

本.meaning: Someone nails a short <part>one</part>-plank bar low on a <part>tree</part> trunk, right where the roots begin, and carves one line of words into it each day. Years later the whole tree is covered in writing. It has turned into a <kanji>book</kanji>.
本.on: A goose with a <sound>hon</sound>king voice sits on the plank and reads the tree out loud.
本.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le digs down to where the roots begin and finds a tiny <sound>to</sound>tem buried at the very origin of the tree.

生.meaning: A stem pushes up out of a flat line of ground, sprouting one leaf, then another. Water it, sing to it, and it keeps on growing, greener every day. That little sprout is <kanji>life</kanji>.
生.on: Someone locks the sprout inside a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe to keep it alive, but it grows right through the door.
生.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals the gardener, as the sprout bursts out of the safe.

向.meaning: A <part>mouth</part> sits inside a <part>frame</part> like a face at a window, a little <part>slash</part> of an antenna on the roof above. It shouts at the hills: 'Hello over there!' The hills shout back. Whatever the mouth is calling to is far away, out <kanji>yonder</kanji>.
向.on: It holds an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne to its lips like a megaphone to shout even further.
向.kun: Out yonder, a cow turns to face the window and answers with one short '<sound>Mu</sound>!'

山.meaning: Three peaks share one wide base, the middle one poking highest into the clouds. Goats live on the left peak, a hermit on the right, and snow sits on the middle. Together they make one big <kanji>mountain</kanji>.
山.on: On the tallest peak, the hermit builds a <sound>sun</sound>dae as big as a snowdrift.
山.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>, <sound>Ma</sound>, I made it!' shouts a goat from the very top of the mountain.

出.meaning: A small <part>mountain</part> rises out of a <part>bucket</part>, and a single trail climbs straight up through both. Hikers squeeze in at the bottom of the bucket and keep going until they pop out of the very top peak: the only way out, the mountain's <kanji>exit</kanji>.
出.on: Climbers sliding out of the exit land in a heap of <sound>su</sound>gar and sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
出.kun: Out you come onto a sunny wooden <sound>de</sound>ck at the foot of the mountain.

刀.meaning: A blade bends down at a sharp corner and sweeps away to the left, as if it was swung so hard it bent. A knight picks it up anyway, straightens it with his boot and charges. It's his trusty <kanji>sword</kanji>.
刀.on: He drops it on his <sound>toe</sound> and hops around the castle yelling.
刀.kun: Then a samurai turns up with a gleaming <sound>katana</sound>, and the knight hides his bent one behind his back.

分.meaning: A pie sits on the table. A <part>sword</part> slices straight up through it, and the two halves fly apart like an <part>eight</part> over the blade. Everyone grabs a <kanji>part</kanji>.
分.on: A ba<sound>boon</sound> swings down from the lamp and steals the biggest part.
分.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' you wail, and then you understand: the baboon took your half.
